candidates.title: INTELLIGENT CAD/CAM INTEGRATION FOR ADAPTIVE MANUFACTURING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF AI AND IOT FRAMEWORKS IN INDUSTRY 4.0
candidates.abstract: The union of Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming the way Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) systems are used in the Industry 4.0 production process. Based on the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework (Page et al., 2021), this report is a systematic literature review on the intelligent integration of CAD and CAM technologies in adaptive manufacturing. Based on a structured search of major scientific databases, a curated list of peer-reviewed studies was analysed thematically to address five research questions related to designing with AI, toolpath optimisation using AI, IoT/IIoT architectures for real-time adaptive control, interoperability standards and barriers to AI adoption in specific sectors. AI models, especially deep learning, graph neural networks and reinforcement learning, have led the way in recent research and development on automatic feature recognition and toolpath generation, while digital twins, edge computing and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) sensor networks are more and more being used to implement predictive maintenance and closed-loop adaptive control in the shop floor. The design phase is also starting to change with Generative AI to enable manufacturability constraints to be built in earlier in the CAD process. The literature, however, shows that there are still significant gaps that need to be addressed: AI models deployed outside of the simulation environment are not adaptable in real-time, training datasets are not standardized and openly shared, and there are interoperability protocols that are still quite disjointed, and resources for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) looking to use these technologies are still limited. To situate these gaps in a particular developing-economy context, this review is also supplemented by a series of recently published empirical studies. The review suggests that interoperability standards, Human Safety for Industry 5.0 design principles, cybersecurity, and sustainable practice are the key factors that need to be coordinated for the intelligent CAD/CAM-IoT integration to be fully realised, and it presents a roadmap of future research directions for adaptive and connected manufacturing ecosystems.

candidates.title: Research on Blended Teaching Reform of Engineering Drawing Course Empowered by AI Application on the BOPPPS Model
candidates.abstract: With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence technology, higher education is undergoing a profound transformation from the traditional “teacher-student” dual structure to a “teacher-AI-student” triadic structure. As a core course for logistics major, Engineering Drawing faces practical challenges such as insufficient student engagement due to the widespread use of AI tools. Based on the BOPPPS teaching model, this study takes the “Logistics Engineering CAD” course of the Logistics Management major at Shenzhen Technology University as an example, and constructs a blended teaching model with triadic collaboration among teachers, AI, and students. This paper elaborates on the role positioning and collaborative mechanisms of teachers, AI, and students in three stages—pre-class, in-class, and post-class—and demonstrates the implementation pathway of AI-empowered teaching through specific course chapters, providing a referable practical framework for the intelligent teaching reform of engineering practice-oriented courses.

candidates.title: CAD-WAM: Anticipating Geometry for Text-to-CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generating editable computer-aided design (CAD) models from text requires selecting operations that produce the intended changes to the geometry constructed so far. An incorrect operation can compromise subsequent steps, making reliable multi-step generation challenging. Existing methods based on large language models (LLMs) primarily learn to predict commands, without explicit supervision of the geometric states those commands should produce. Inspired by world-action models, we introduce CAD-WAM, which couples geometry-conditioned action generation with next-state prediction. We define complete modeling operations as actions in a CAD domain-specific language (DSL) and encode surface point clouds of intermediate solids into compact latent states using a pretrained variational autoencoder. An LLM backbone generates the next action from the target description and current geometric state, while an auxiliary head on the same backbone predicts the next state to provide geometric supervision during training. We construct step-wise training trajectories from parametric CAD models in the DeepCAD dataset, pairing each trajectory with an expert-level textual description. At inference, each generated action is executed by a CAD kernel, and the resulting solid is re-encoded to inform the next decision. On the DeepCAD test set, CAD-WAM outperforms the task-specific baselines in geometric accuracy and output validity, with larger gains on models requiring more operations, and produces more accurate geometry than general-purpose LLMs prompted with the same DSL. Ablations further show that next-state supervision reduces mean Chamfer distance by 13.2\% relative to an otherwise identical model trained only to predict actions. Code is available at https://github.com/Lzy-1037/CAD-WAM.

candidates.title: Co-Construction of Production-Line AAS Geometric Models and Knowledge Graphs Driven by a Vision-Language Model
candidates.abstract: Digital twin systems for a production line usually run on two models at once: an Asset Administration Shell (AAS) that holds asset information under IEC 63278, and a knowledge graph (KG) that records device topology and process semantics. On real projects, though, the two are built apart from each other. Engineers key the AAS geometric model in by hand from drawings and field measurements, while process engineers author the KG separately. The same data therefore gets entered twice, reuse is poor, and sooner or later the two models disagree. This paper presents a co-construction method that removes the duplication at its source. A fine-tuned vision-language model (VLM) reads the engineering sources a line already has, namely 2D/3D CAD drawings, on-site laser point clouds, and equipment technical manuals, and fills a standardized AAS; the KG is then derived from that AAS by fixed rules, so both models share one source. The method is arranged in four layers: multi-source data preprocessing with coarse-to-fine ICP spatial registration; LoRA-based domain adaptation of an open-source VLM supported by industrial prompt templates; automatic population of the AAS geometric, property, and connectivity submodels with conformance-checked .aasx generation on Eclipse BaSyx, plus QEM-based mesh simplification; and same-source KG derivation through fixed field-to-triple mapping rules, backed by a single-source constraint, automatic reconciliation, and incremental refresh with version traceability. We demonstrate the complete pipeline on a photovoltaic cell production line, and a parameterized Monte Carlo simulation of data consistency shows that, for manual single-entry error rates between 1% and 10%, conventional dual-entry modeling produces 4–39 times more data inconsistencies than the proposed single-source derivation, with the gap widening as the error rate grows. The method offers a reusable and extensible path toward production-line digital twin modeling; empirical validation on a physical line is planned as future work.

candidates.title: Automation of Tunnel Support Detailing with AI-Assisted Programming
candidates.abstract: Drafting tasks in geological engineering are time-consuming and often highly repetitive, with tunnel support drawings being a representative example. Although such tasks may appear straightforward and intuitive to experienced engineers, translating drafting logic into executable code typically requires substantial software development effort. While modern CAD and BIM platforms provide programming and automation capabilities, their effective use has traditionally depended on skilled programmers rather than domain engineers. This paper presents a practical case study in which a geological engineer with only basic programming experience leveraged recent advances in artificial intelligence, specifically large language models, to develop a custom code for automating tunnel support drawings. The workflow generates detailed support layouts directly from the tunnel contour and a limited set of user-defined engineering parameters, such as bolt spacing, liner thickness, and support class. Crucially, the approach preserves engineering judgement by requiring the engineer to define all design parameters and to review the final outputs, while automating repetitive drafting operations. The results demonstrate a viable pathway for lowering the barrier to engineering automation. The proposed approach is readily extendable to similar repetitive drawing tasks across a broad range of geological engineering applications.

candidates.title: Single-Image 3D Mesh Reconstruction via Point-Aware Diffusion (SPAR3D) and Bezier Spline Vectorization (SVG/EPS/DXF) for Engineering and Industrial Design Education
candidates.abstract: Abstract (ERIC 5-Element Standard): The purpose of this study is to evaluate browser-based single-image three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction and raster-to-vector contour tracing for computer-aided design (CAD), rapid prototyping, and additive manufacturing instruction. The methodology examines Stable Point-Aware 3D (SPAR3D) architecture—which couples point-cloud diffusion sampling with triplane mesh reconstruction—across 50 object categories (DS-3), alongside cubic Bezier spline quantization into Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG), Encapsulated PostScript (EPS), and Drawing Exchange Format (DXF) for computer numerical control (CNC) laser cutting. Results demonstrate that SPAR3D reconstructs watertight textured 3D meshes averaging 42,500 to 61,500 vertices in a mean inference time of 6.20 seconds directly in a web browser, while vector tracing reduces geometric contour error below 0.42 pixels. By offloading neural point-cloud generation from local workstations to browser endpoints, vocational and engineering programs eliminate the requirement for 24-gigabyte VRAM GPUs. Implications for STEM and CTE curricula include accessible 2D-to-3D fabrication workflows. Additional materials include 6 tables, 34 references, CAD lab protocols, and 190 embedded URI links. candidates.title: CardioHolisticAI for multimodal deep learning based coronary artery disease risk stratification and personalized treatment recommendation
candidates.abstract: Despite the significant reduction in mortality and morbidity caused by coronary artery disease (CAD), early stratification of risk is important for timely intervention and individualised care. Most current CAD prediction methods rely on clinical variables, focus on single-modality analysis or simple fusion, and lack interpretability, calibration, and robustness assessment. The authors introduce CardioHolisticAI, a multimodal deep learning framework that also features MultiRiskNet for CAD risk stratification in Low, Medium, and High risk. MultiRiskNet leverages modality-specific encoders and attention-guided fusion to combine clinical features, modality-agnostic radiomic descriptors, and genomic pathway information while maintaining modality-specific representations. A multilevel explainability module integrates SHAP-based global importance, Integrated Gradients-based local attribution, radiomic feature ranking, and pathway-level genomic analysis. MultiRiskNet was evaluated with repeated five-fold cross-validation and achieved an accuracy of 98.50 ± 0.16%, a Macro-F1 score of 0.985 ± 0.0015, and a one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 0.992 ± 0.0009, outperforming all evaluated unimodal and conventional fusion baselines. Noise injection, feature masking, and repeated-initialisation experiments suggest stable performance under the assessed internal conditions, and calibration analysis examined the reliability of the predicted probabilities. This is because the imaging source is non-cardiac and the source modalities are independent and not clinically validated at the patient level. Before clinical deployment, external evaluation in a patient-linked multimodal cardiac cohort is needed.
